Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese is set to visit Beijing next month, seeking to stabilize the nations’ relationship, the South China Morning Post reportedBloomberg Terminal
, citing unidentified people.
Albanese will head to the capital after attending the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation leaders’ summit in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen on Nov. 18 and 19, the English-language newspaper said. The prime minister last visited Beijing in July and the next trip would be his third to the city since taking office in 2022, according to the report.

Wall Street got a reality check as a bruising selloff in technology shares fueled concern the artificial-intelligence frenzy that has powered the equity bull market might be overblown.
Disappointing tech results spurred the worst drop for stocks since June, with the Nasdaq 100 sinking 3.5% and briefly crossing the threshold of a technical correction. Intel Corp. slid the most in over four decades. The S&P 500 fell 1.8%, breaching its 100-day moving average.

item.title: Chocolate Price Spook Families for Halloween
item.description:
BusinessWeek Radio Simulcast • Oct 30th, 2026
Chocolate Price Spook Families for Halloween
Halloween candy is getting more expensive as higher labor, energy and transportation costs continue to pressure food prices. Stew Leonard Jr., CEO of Stew Leonard’s, says bags of popular candy are up about 50 cents from last year, prompting some shoppers to trade down to cheaper options. He joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss how affordability is changing consumer behavior, and how both environmental and economic changes are impacting the business.

item.title: Crypto Hack Reignites Regulatory Debate
item.description:
BusinessWeek Radio Simulcast • Oct 30th, 2026
Crypto Hack Reignites Regulatory Debate
A $6 billion crypto hack is putting digital-asset security back in the spotlight. Former CFTC chairman J. Christopher Giancarlo, known as “CryptoDad”, argues the attack exposed vulnerabilities at an individual firm rather than a failure of underlying blockchain technology. He is also calling for the US to take a more aggressive approach to state-sponsored cyberattacks. He joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss the fallout from the hack and why he believes prediction markets should be regulated federally by the CFTC rather than by individual states.

item.title: PacSun CEO: Brands Mean a Lot to Young People Today
item.description:
Bloomberg The Close • Oct 30th, 2026
PacSun CEO: Brands Mean a Lot to Young People Today
Brieane Olson, CEO of PacSun, says that the retailer’s core customer is 16 to 24, while it is also tracking differences between Gen Z and Gen Alpha. Drawing on a PacSun Youth Report conducted with GlobalData and surveying 6,000 young people, Olson said mental health ranks as their top priority. She cited PACSUN’s ongoing partnership with Selena Gomez and the Rare Impact Foundation as an example of collaborations intended to have lasting value for young customers. She speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close" on October 29, 2026.

item.title: Ice Cube on Big3 League: In a Great Position To Scale
item.description:
Bloomberg The Close • Oct 30th, 2026
Ice Cube on Big3 League: In a Great Position To Scale
Ice Cube, CEO & Co-Founder of the Big3 basketball league, says audiences want more basketball in the summer and argues that the league has helped professionalize three-on-three play. He describes basketball as a globally beloved sport and say the league is well positioned to grow, noting that it is already recognized as the world’s premier professional three-on-three league. He speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close" on October 29, 2026.

item.title: Investor Looks to Bid on Club Pilates-Owner Xponential
item.description: Fund 1 Investments LLC, the third-largest shareholder in Xponential Fitness Inc., the owner of Club Pilates and Pure Barre brands, said it’s pushing for a take-private and is looking to buy the company itself.

item.title: Brazil Summons Argentine Envoy Over Role in Bolsonaro’s Escape
item.description: Brazilian authorities summoned Argentina’s top envoy in the country on Friday to explain President Javier Milei’s role in helping Flávio Bolsonaro flee Brazil following his election defeat.

item.title: Wall Street Boom to Cut New York State Budget Deficit in Half
item.description: New York projected the budget deficit will narrow by $3.5 billion next year as the state expects a boom in trading and borrowing to deliver record profits to Wall Street and stronger bonus payments to boost revenue.
